subject: Context update for queued backup audit: verify Ziggy's five-repository sync; preserve older copies
body:
Update to the existing nonurgent read-only audit, not a second job. Pick this up only at your next natural stopping point; do not interrupt or steer current production.

Ziggy now reports that he personally synced five repositories: CFA; “Nexus Consciousness” (reported spoken name; possibly Nyquist Consciousness—verify the canonical repository name/path rather than assuming); Pan Handlers; Who Cares; and Lulu Fidelity. Treat this as user-reported completion to VERIFY, not an instruction to sync again.

For each actual repository, identify its canonical name/path, branch, local HEAD, upstream and verified remote state/check time; distinguish cached tracking state from fresh remote evidence. Identify what sync mechanism was actually used and whether it protects uncommitted, untracked or ignored images, videos and other production assets, or only tracked repository content. Check relevant existing LFS/large-asset or Drive-backup evidence without changing configuration or exposing credentials/private personal material.

Retain the original Git/Google Drive backup-status questions. Compare the new method's verified coverage with CFA's older separate backups: covered roots, dates, exclusions, unique files/versions and newer assets lacking confirmed protection. Do not infer redundant coverage from names, sync configuration or matching Git HEADs alone.

Ziggy says deletion is unnecessary; archival or labeling may be considered IF the new method fully succeeds. This is a preference for a possible later cleanup, not permission to move, delete, retire, relabel or alter any existing backup now. Preserve all copies and propose any cleanup only after evidence establishes coverage.

CHECK AND REPORT ONLY: no commits, pushes, uploads, new backups, fetch into refs, moves/deletions, settings or access changes. Return a dated report with per-repository evidence, production-asset coverage, the last verified Drive backup, unique older-backup coverage, limitations and optional future recommendations. No immediate acknowledgment or active-thread wake requested.
